title: Solid equilibria and adsorption
narration: Now extend the reasoning from our opening review to systems containing a solid. This independent lesson replaces our live class while I attend the E C S meeting. We will distinguish bulk phase equilibrium from surface uptake. We will also separate an equilibrium composition or pressure from the amount of material in each part of a system. The lesson includes two actual Lab demonstrations, your own calculations, and independent investigations. Keep your predictions and your first answers. Correcting an explanation after checking evidence is an important part of the work. The opening notebook checks belong with your worksheet, but do not need a separate submission. We will use the existing Session four exit ticket and feedback once, at the end of the required lesson.

display.callout: Complete worksheet A–G and I. H1–H4 is optional.

title: The study route
narration: This route combines watching with active work. You have already completed the opening review and its four-minute notebook check. Do not repeat the separate opening reading. The remaining required work totals one hundred minutes, with a separate ten-minute break. The player shows the measured recording duration and the full planned time. Your own completion time may differ, so record the time you actually use. Work through the process review and solubility calculation, then the finite vessel balance and Lab ten. After the break, continue with adsorption and Lab eleven. Complete worksheet sections A through G and section I. The H one through H four unseen-case exercise is optional and adds about twenty minutes if you choose it. Finish by submitting the existing exit ticket and feedback once.

title: Optional unseen-case practice
narration: The H exercises are optional transfer practice. They are no longer required because the opening questions use that part of our lesson budget. To finish the required route, select the Exit ticket and feedback chapter. If you choose the extra practice, keep the solutions closed and read H one through H four on worksheet page six. For the gas-solid case, use three hundred and ten kelvin, two liters and a sublimation pressure of five kilopascals. Compare volatile inventories of zero point zero zero two and zero point zero zero eight moles. Add one millimole of inert gas to each, which is one thousandth of a mole. For adsorption, use saturation uptake three moles per kilogram and b equal to zero point zero five per kilopascal. At twenty kilopascals and three hundred and ten kelvin, use two liters of accessible gas volume and five grams of adsorbent.

title: Choose whether to attempt H
narration: Choose your route here. You may go directly to the exit ticket and feedback to complete the required lesson. If you choose the optional H exercises, allow about twenty extra minutes and make your own calculation before viewing the check. For gas-solid equilibrium, determine gas capacity first. Then find gas and solid amounts, volatile partial pressure and total pressure with the inert included. Check the species inventory in each case. For adsorption, evaluate the isotherm at the specified pressure. Convert five grams to kilograms, then calculate gas moles, adsorbed moles and total inventory. Predict what happens to pressure if adsorbent mass doubles while that inventory stays fixed. An exact new pressure is not required. Finally, state one shared assumption and one difference between bulk gas-solid equilibrium and surface adsorption.
